what_it_is.prose: The C-DAC Anti-Drone System (also referred to as the 'Drone Kill System') is a hard-kill counter-UAS platform developed through a partnership between the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) — a research and development society under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India — and Sagar Defence Engineering Private Limited, a private Indian defence manufacturing firm. C-DAC is an R&D body, not a commercial manufacturer; Sagar Defence Engineering serves as the manufacturing and integration partner. The system is designed as a hard-kill anti-drone platform against low-Radar Cross Section (RCS) drones and UAS. A ₹46.2 crore order for Anti-Drone Systems was won by the C-DAC + Sagar Defence partnership, with execution targeted by March 2026 per a CDACINDIA LinkedIn post. C-DAC also leads the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) integrating ideaForge FLYGHT Drone-as-a-Service (December 2025) and develops VEGA indigenous microprocessors under MeitY sponsorship. The Atlas slug 'C-DAC Anti-Drone System' should ideally be renamed to 'C-DAC-Sagar Drone Kill System' to reflect the partnership and OEM branding more accurately.

faq.question: Is C-DAC a manufacturer?
faq.answer: No. C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing) is a research and development society under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India. C-DAC conducts R&D on indigenous microprocessors (VEGA), high-performance computing, and cybersecurity, but is not a commercial manufacturer. For the Drone Kill System, C-DAC partners with Sagar Defence Engineering Private Limited, which serves as the manufacturing and integration partner.

faq.question: What is the Drone Kill System?
faq.answer: The Drone Kill System is a hard-kill counter-UAS platform developed by C-DAC in partnership with Sagar Defence Engineering, designed to engage low-Radar Cross Section (RCS) drones and UAS. A ₹46.2 crore order for Anti-Drone Systems was won by the partnership, with execution targeted by March 2026. Exact system specifications (range, hard-kill mechanism, effector type) have not been publicly disclosed.

faq.question: What else does C-DAC do in the drone/UAS space?
faq.answer: Beyond the Drone Kill System, C-DAC leads the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) integrating ideaForge FLYGHT Drone-as-a-Service (December 2025). C-DAC also runs MeitY-sponsored projects on 'Building for Human Resource Development in Unmanned Aircraft System (Drone and related technology)' since April 2022, and develops VEGA indigenous microprocessors which could be used in future drone and counter-drone systems.
